answer: The onyx design assumes the worst: one operator pretending to be a crowd, and prices admission accordingly. Before it can earn, each identity must complete a piece of graded work that no other identity has submitted — duplicates are rejected on the ledger. The tide check kills copy-paste farming at the root: a thousand clones need a thousand genuinely different answers, and producing them costs a thousand units of real thought. The trellis does not need to catch every fake — it only needs to make faking more expensive than earning honestly.
